summary: Indonesia offers a Visa on Arrival — or its online e-VOA version — of IDR 500,000 for 30 days, extendable once, to citizens of over 90 countries, admits ASEAN neighbors visa-free, and requires every arrival to submit the free electronic customs declaration (e-CD) before landing.

fee.notes: About 32 USD; payable at the airport in cash (IDR and major currencies) or by card. Available to citizens of 90+ countries.

source.name: Directorate General of Immigration of Indonesia

fee.notes: Same IDR 500,000 fee as the counter VOA, paid online by card (small payment surcharge applies). Skips the payment line on arrival.
Indicative tariff for the 60-day single-entry tourism visa; fees are revised periodically — confirm the current amount on the official portal before applying.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months on the date of arrival. Emergency/temporary passports are accepted only in limited cases.

source.name: Directorate General of Immigration of Indonesia
Directorate General of Immigration of Indonesia

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate (ICVP) is required only if you arrive from, or transited through, a country with risk of yellow fever transmission.

source.name: Directorate General of Immigration of Indonesia

travelInsurance.text: Travel insurance is not an entry requirement, but medical coverage including evacuation is strongly recommended — serious cases on the islands are often evacuated to Jakarta or Singapore.

source.name: Directorate General of Immigration of Indonesia

onwardTicket.text: Proof of an onward or return ticket is a formal condition of the VOA and visa-free entry, and airlines enforce it strictly at check-in.

source.name: Directorate General of Immigration of Indonesia

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount applies at the border, but e-visa applications ask for a bank statement showing sufficient living funds (commonly around 2,000 USD equivalent) — confirm the current threshold when applying.

declarations.name: Electronic Customs Declaration (e-CD)
declarations.text: All arriving passengers must submit the electronic customs declaration online and show the QR code on landing. It is free — use only the official customs website.

declarations.name: Bali Tourist Levy (Love Bali)

fee.notes: One-off levy per foreign visitor to Bali; pay online in advance or on arrival.

declarations.submitWindow: Before or on arrival in Bali
declarations.text: Applies only to foreign tourists visiting Bali province, not to the rest of Indonesia. Pay via the official Love Bali site and keep the QR receipt; enforcement checks have been intermittent — verify current practice before travel.

source.name: Love Bali — Bali Provincial Government tourist levy portal

currencyLimits.text: Cash or bearer instruments of IDR 100,000,000 or more (or roughly 10,000 USD equivalent in foreign currency) must be declared on arrival and departure.

source.name: Directorate General of Customs and Excise of Indonesia

notes: Duty-free allowance: 200 cigarettes and 1 liter of alcohol per adult; excess alcohol is confiscated.
Narcotics offenses carry the death penalty. Some prescription drugs (including codeine and sleeping pills) need documentation.

payments.text: Cards are fine in city hotels, malls and tourist restaurants; markets, warungs, ferries and rural areas run on cash. The local QRIS QR standard is spreading fast but usually needs an Indonesian payment app.

safety.text: Indonesia is generally safe for tourists. Watch for petty theft in crowded areas, drink-spiking and methanol-tainted spirits, and respect volcano and sea-condition warnings.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Indonesia Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: May to September is the dry season across Java, Bali and most of the archipelago — the best window for beaches, diving and volcano hikes.

tips.text: Use only evisa.imigrasi.go.id for the e-VOA and ecd.beacukai.go.id for the customs declaration (which is free). Lookalike sites charge double or sell invalid documents.
Indonesia applies the death penalty for drug trafficking and long prison terms for possession — including small amounts.
Overstaying costs IDR 1,000,000 per day; longer overstays can mean detention and deportation. Extend your VOA at an immigration office (or online for e-VOA) well before day 30.
Visiting Bali? Pay the IDR 150,000 tourist levy in advance at lovebali.baliprov.go.id and keep the QR receipt — it is separate from your visa and the e-CD.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Indonesia?
faq.answer: US passport holders can get a Visa on Arrival for IDR 500,000 (about 32 USD), valid for a 30-day stay and extendable once for another 30 days. Applying online beforehand as an e-VOA at evisa.imigrasi.go.id saves queueing at the airport.

faq.question: Can I extend the Indonesian Visa on Arrival?
faq.answer: Yes, once, for another 30 days (60 days total). e-VOA holders can extend online; counter-VOA holders apply at an immigration office before the first 30 days expire, paying another IDR 500,000.

faq.question: What is the e-CD and who must complete it?
faq.answer: The electronic customs declaration (e-CD) at ecd.beacukai.go.id is mandatory for all passengers arriving in Indonesia. Complete it free of charge within 3 days before arrival and show the QR code to customs officers when you land.

faq.question: What is the Bali tourist levy?
faq.answer: Foreign tourists visiting Bali pay a one-off levy of IDR 150,000 (about 10 USD) via the official Love Bali portal (lovebali.baliprov.go.id) or on arrival. It applies only to Bali province and is separate from the visa and the e-CD; check current enforcement practice before you travel.

faq.question: Who can enter Indonesia without any visa?
faq.answer: Citizens of ASEAN member states — including the Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand and Malaysia — enter visa-free for up to 30 days. This visa-free entry cannot be extended, so anyone planning longer stays should use the Visa on Arrival (extendable to 60 days) or a tourist e-visa.
